questions.question: The turning point of y = 2(x + 3)² − 8 is:
In the bracket (x + 3), the graph has been moved:
options: Three units left — opposite to the visible sign
Not at all; only q moves the graph

questions.question: The x-intercepts of y = 2(x + 3)² − 8 are:
options: x = −5 and x = −1, balancing about the axis x = −3

questions.question: The range of y = 2(x + 3)² − 8 is:
options: y ≥ −8 — the minimum is genuinely reached

questions.question: The asymptotes of y = 4/(x + 1) − 2 are:
With a = 4 (positive), the two branches occupy:
options: The top-left and bottom-right corners of the asymptote cross
The top-right and bottom-left corners of the asymptote cross

questions.question: The intercepts of y = 4/(x + 1) − 2 are:
The domain of y = 4/(x + 1) − 2 must be written as:
options: All real x except x = −1 — a domain without its exception is a different graph

subtopics.title: The Exponential Graph Raised and Shifted

questions.question: The horizontal asymptote of y = 4 · 2^(x−1) − 8 is:
The y-intercept of y = 4 · 2^(x−1) − 8 is:
Solving 4 · 2^(x−1) − 8 = 0 for the x-intercept gives:
options: x = 2 — from 2^(x−1) = 2, matching powers of the common base

questions.question: The range of y = 4 · 2^(x−1) − 8 is:
options: y > −8 — strictly, because the graph never lands on its asymptote

subtopics.title: Average Gradient and the Slope of a Curve

questions.question: The average gradient of a curve between two points is:
options: The gradient of the straight line joining the two points
The sum of the gradients at both points

questions.question: On y = x², the average gradient between x = 2 and x = 4 is:
Fixing x = 2 and shrinking the interval gave averages 5; 4,5; 4,1 — approaching:
options: 4 — the gradient of the curve at the point x = 2

questions.question: The wording 'the gradient of the curve AT x = 2' signals:
options: An average between two given points
A limit — the destination of shrinking-interval averages

questions.question: In the tent picture, the q in the equation is:
options: The crane — it hoists or lowers the whole tent without changing its shape

questions.question: The reliable way to read the bracket's sideways push is to ask:
options: What x makes the bracket zero — that is where the low point now stands

questions.question: A negative a does what to the tent?
options: Inverts it — the lowest point becomes a highest point

questions.question: The x-intercepts −5 and −1 confirm the centre pole because:
options: They average to −3, the axis of symmetry

questions.question: An asymptote is best described as:
options: A fence the graph presses against forever without touching
A line the graph crosses once

questions.question: The hyperbola's vertical fence stands where:
options: The denominator would divide by zero

questions.question: The exponential has exactly one fence because:
options: b to any power is strictly positive, so only the height q is unreachable — x is never restricted

questions.question: Touch versus approach: which range carries the equals sign?
options: The exponential's — it reaches its floor
The parabola's — it genuinely touches its turning point; the exponential only approaches

questions.question: A bakkie covers 240 km between tollgates in 3 hours. Its average speed is:
options: 80 km/h — one honest number summarising a varying trip
Impossible to know without the speedometer

questions.question: On a graph, the average gradient between two points is pictured as:
options: The tangent at the first point
A taut string joining the two points

questions.question: As the second tollgate slides towards x = 2 on y = x², the string gradients 5; 4,5; 4,1 converge on:
options: 4 — the speedometer reading at the instant x = 2

questions.question: In exam wording, 'between' and 'at' signal:
options: 'Between' = the string (direct calculation); 'at' = the limit of shrinking averages
